clue.text: City in Michigan disposing of old 19's rubbish

indicators.note: a city disposing of something gets rid of it, so a letter is taken out of the city's name

parts.note: Detroit is the largest city in the US state of Michigan
the answer to 19 is AMERICAN, and US is the abbreviation for American

explanation.surface: A Michigan city is clearing away its old American junk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposing of' removes O (old) from DETROIT, leaving DETRIT; the cross-reference to 19 gives US.
explanation.definitionFit: Detritus is debris or waste matter, so it is a synonym of rubbish.

clue.text: Bishop leaves behind time in high spirits

indicators.note: the bishop leaves, meaning his letter departs from the phrase that follows

parts.note: something done behind time is done late, i.e. belatedly
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop departs late, leaving time behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes B (Bishop) out of BELATEDLY, which means behind time.
explanation.definitionFit: Elatedly means joyfully or exultantly, which is acting in high spirits.

clue.text: Location of round posters seen during car trip?

indicators.note: things seen during a trip appear in the middle of it, so these pieces go inside the word for trip

parts.note: a ride is a trip in a car
O is round in shape
posters are advertisements, ads

explanation.surface: Where would you see round posters on a car journey?
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside is a place beside the road, a location where hoardings stand.

clue.text: Think of the old days, having no bridge in town

indicators.note: the town is shown having no bridge, so that word is struck from its name

parts.note: Trowbridge is the county town of Wiltshire, in England
taken as written, the second half of the town's name

explanation.surface: Someone reminisces about a town that lacks a bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: TROWBRIDGE is the county town of Wiltshire; dropping BRIDGE leaves the archaic verb. 'of the old days' marks the definition as archaic.
explanation.definitionFit: Trow is an archaic verb meaning to believe or think.

clue.text: Rest day's rating in southern city

indicators.note: the rating sits in the southern city, so his letters go inside it

parts.note: Bath is an English city in Somerset
an AB (able seaman) is a naval rating

explanation.surface: A sailor spends his day off in a city in the south of England.
explanation.walkthrough: AB goes inside S + BATH; the 's in 'day's' stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest in Jewish and Christian observance.

clue.text: Food item athlete eats initially in bar

parts.note: a runner is a track athlete

indicators.note: that letter goes inside the word for bar

parts.note: to bar is to ban

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word eats

explanation.surface: An athlete takes a snack at the start of a session in the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner bean is a climbing bean whose pods are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Horse a satirical author used to reach Japanese port

parts.note: a nag is an old horse
Saki was the pen name of H. H. Munro, a satirical short-story writer

explanation.surface: A satirist rides a horse to reach a port in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagasaki is a major port city on the Japanese island of Kyushu.

clue.text: Snake on stream showing evidence of exposure

parts.note: to snake is to wind, as a path does
a burn is a Scottish word for a stream

explanation.surface: A snake slithers along a stream, out in the open.
explanation.walkthrough: BURN is the Scottish word for a small stream.
explanation.definitionFit: Windburn is skin reddening caused by long exposure to wind, a sign of being out in the elements.

clue.text: University graduate backing race, say, in Arab state

indicators.note: backing turns the university and graduate letters round so they read in reverse

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

indicators.note: say signals that a word spoken aloud gives the letters

parts.note: the Derby is a famous English horse race, pronounced DAR-bee in Britain

explanation.surface: A university graduate puts money on a race in the Gulf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns U + BA into ABU; 'say' makes DERBY, said the British way, sound like DHABI.
explanation.definitionFit: Abu Dhabi is one of the emirates of the United Arab Emirates, and its capital.

clue.text: Pet grooming implement found outside a burial chamber

indicators.note: the pet and the implement are found outside the a, so it goes between them

parts.note: a cat is a common pet
a comb is used for grooming hair or fur

explanation.surface: A pet comb turns up outside a tomb.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery, a chamber or gallery for burying the dead.

clue.text: An unmarried slave, Pussy Galore?

definitions.meaning: a young woman held in servitude, a female bondservant
Pussy Galore is a woman in a James Bond story

explanation.walkthrough: Pussy Galore is a character in the James Bond novel and film Goldfinger; the question mark flags the pun.
explanation.definitionFit: A bondmaid is a female slave or bondservant, and a Bond girl is punningly a Bond maid.

clue.text: Manage to change Radio Times, swapping old for new

indicators.note: to change the title is to rearrange its letters
swapping one letter for another replaces the old letter with the new one

explanation.surface: An editor plans to revamp the Radio Times, replacing old features with new.
explanation.walkthrough: In RADIO TIMES replace O (old) with N (new), then 'to change' rearranges RADNITIMES. Radio Times is a British TV and radio listings magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to manage or run an organisation or affairs.

clue.text: Vessel useful at beginning of party?

definitions.meaning: a ship built to cut a channel through frozen seas
a game or remark that gets strangers talking when a gathering starts

explanation.definitionFit: Icebreakers are both ships that clear ice and activities that relax people at a social event.

clue.text: Forbidden return of upper-class sportsman

indicators.note: the return of the pieces means they read backwards

parts.note: a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: An upper-class athlete is barred from coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns U + BAT round. BAT for batsman is a cricket usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabu is a variant spelling of taboo, meaning prohibited.

clue.text: The sort destined to work as a compositor

parts.note: a sort is a type or kind
set means fixed or destined, as in set to win

explanation.surface: Someone of that kind is bound for a printing job.
explanation.walkthrough: A compositor sets type by hand for printing.
explanation.definitionFit: To typeset is to arrange type for printing, which is a compositor's work.

clue.text: Having a lute, get free instruction

indicators.note: setting the letters free lets them be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone who owns a lute gets lessons without paying.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is teaching or tuition given by a tutor.

clue.text: Floorboards in sketch drawn with ruler

parts.note: a plan is a sketch or outline drawing
a king is a ruler

explanation.surface: Floorboards are drawn in a sketch using a ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' wants to be a measuring stick in this drawing scene; it is a monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Planking is boards or planks collectively, such as those laid as a floor.

clue.text: East End plant overwhelmed by Welsh girl's language!

indicators.note: something overwhelmed by another is engulfed by it, so it goes inside

parts.note: Sian is a Welsh girl's name
Cockneys of London's East End drop the H, so herb becomes 'erb

explanation.surface: A Welsh girl swears at a Cockney gardener.
explanation.walkthrough: 'language!' looks like a reaction to swearing, but it is the definition. East End (Cockney) speech drops the H from herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Serbian is the South Slavic language spoken in Serbia.

clue.text: Black reptile unknown to appear in this awful weather

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: an unknown that appears in something is placed within it

parts.note: a lizard is a reptile
Z is a mathematical unknown, like x and y

explanation.surface: A black lizard emerges unexpectedly in a snowstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: A blizzard is a severe snowstorm with strong winds, certainly awful weather.

clue.text: A bloke going round Morecambe like Buffalo Bill

indicators.note: the bloke goes round the comedian, enclosing his name

parts.note: a bloke is a man
Eric Morecambe was a much-loved British comedian

explanation.surface: A man wanders round the seaside town of Morecambe dressed as a cowboy.
explanation.walkthrough: Morecambe is also a Lancashire seaside town, but here it is the comedian Eric Morecambe.
explanation.definitionFit: Buffalo Bill Cody was a US showman, so he was American.

clue.text: Holiday-maker holding up spades and scuttle

indicators.note: in a down answer the holiday-maker holds up the spade from below, so it sits on top

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades
a camper is someone holidaying in a tent

explanation.surface: A camper with spades runs off.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper is to run quickly with small steps, like a scuttle.

clue.text: Gin some knocked back

indicators.note: knocked back means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: part means some of something

explanation.surface: Someone downs a measure of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' wants to be the drink, matching 'knocked back'; it is a gin trap for animals.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin is a snare or trap for catching animals.

clue.text: Think again about clause covering key Tories

indicators.note: the clause covers the other pieces, wrapping round them

parts.note: a rider is a clause added to a document
E is a musical key
Cons is short for Conservatives, the Tories

explanation.surface: A clause concerning major Tory figures prompts a rethink.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider something is to think it over again.

clue.text: Apathetic doctor beginning to moan about engagements

parts.note: St Luke was a physician
military engagements make up war

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: An indifferent doctor starts grumbling about his appointments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' links the pieces: M ends up after WAR. 'engagements' wants appointments; it means battles.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm means lacking enthusiasm, half-hearted, which is apathetic.

clue.text: Description of organ and certain drums?

definitions.text: Description of organ and certain drums?

parts.words: Description of organ and certain drums?
parts.note: an adjective for the organ of hearing, and so for the drums found in that organ

explanation.definitionFit: Otic means relating to the ear, the organ that contains the eardrums.

clue.text: Poet's pressure gets one like Herod Antipas beheaded

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: beheaded means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: Herod Antipas was tetrarch of Galilee, a ruler of a quarter of a province

explanation.surface: A poet is under pressure from a headless Biblical ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: TETRARCH beheaded loses its first T; the 's in 'Poet's' stands for 'has' or 'is'. Herod Antipas ordered John the Baptist beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrarch was a fourteenth-century Italian poet famed for his sonnets.

clue.text: From Swiss, cry of pleasure about snowfields

indicators.note: about means around, so the cry goes round the snowfields

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise or delight
névés are fields of granular snow at the head of glaciers

explanation.surface: A Swiss visitor exclaims with delight at the snowfields.
explanation.walkthrough: NEVE (névé) is granular snow on a glacier; 'From Swiss' reads as 'of a Swiss city' here.
explanation.definitionFit: Genevese means from or of Geneva, the Swiss city.

clue.text: Going back about church bell's sound

parts.note: re means about or concerning
CE is the Church of England
ding is the sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: Someone retreats from a church on hearing its bell.
explanation.definitionFit: Receding means moving back or withdrawing.
